{{nihongo|'''Komori Katte Shrine'''|籠守勝手神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

=== Overview ===
*The founding period is unknown. Since {{ill|Ichinobe no Oshiwa|Q2297842|qid=Q2297842}}, father of Princes Oke and Woke, is said to have been killed by Emperor Yūryaku in {{ill|Emperor Ankō|Q361010|qid=Q361010}} 3 ({{ill|456|Q30432|qid=Q30432}}), it is presumed this shrine had already been founded before then. Kuroda Shrine was the formal name, but it was also called Komori Katte Shrine at that time.
*It was long regarded as an important shrine. There are records of imperial offerings in the reigns of {{ill|Empress Kōken|Q232955|qid=Q232955|lt=Empress Shōtoku}} and {{ill|Emperor Uda|Q349267|qid=Q349267}}, and in {{ill|951|Q23654|qid=Q23654}} ({{ill|Tenryaku|de|Tenryaku|fa|تنریاکو|fr|Ère Tenryaku|hr|Tenryaku|ia|Tenryaku|id|Tenryaku|ja|天暦|ko|덴랴쿠|ru|Тэнряку|sh|Tenryaku|simple|Tenryaku|sr|Тенрјаку|tr|Tenryaku|uk|Тенряку|zh|天曆 (日本)|zh_yue|天曆 (日本)|qid=Q1346281}} 5), an envoy of {{ill|Emperor Murakami|Q374015|qid=Q374015}} prayed there for recovery from illness.
*In {{ill|1582|Q6719|qid=Q6719}} ({{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 10), it was rebuilt by {{ill|Sawai Katsushige|Q11553123|qid=Q11553123}}, lord of {{ill|Kuroda Castle|Q11678587|qid=Q11678587|lt=Kuroda Castle}} and chief retainer of {{ill|Oda Nobukatsu|Q3044815|qid=Q3044815}}.
*In the Edo period it was called “Kuroda Daimyōjin” and “Hakusan Shrine.” When it became gōsha for the northwestern Haguri District area in {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} (Meiji 5), it was renamed Komori Katte Shrine.

=== Mikago Festival ===
A ritual held on lunar August 15. Images of Princes Oke and Woke are placed in {{ill|Kago|Q936754|qid=Q936754}} palanquins, taro is offered, and prayers are made for warding off misfortune and abundant harvest. This derives from the following tradition.

*{{ill|Ichinobe no Oshiwa|Q2297842|qid=Q2297842}}, father of Oke and Woke, was a prince of {{ill|Emperor Richū|Q329704|qid=Q329704}}. {{ill|Emperor Ankō|Q361010|qid=Q361010}} (his nephew) intended to pass the throne to him, but in Ankō 3 ({{ill|456|Q30432|qid=Q30432}}), Ankō was assassinated by {{ill|Prince Mayowa|Q11582590|qid=Q11582590}}. Prince Ōhatsuse (later {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235}}), who had long resented this, lured Ichinobe Oshiwa no Miko to hunting grounds at Kayano in {{ill|Ōmi Province|Q843882|qid=Q843882}} and shot him.
*The brothers Oke (later {{ill|Emperor Ninken|Q357266|qid=Q357266}}) and Woke (later {{ill|Emperor Kenzō|Q360966|qid=Q360966}}), fearing further danger, fled the capital. On their way toward {{ill|Masumida Shrine|Q705916|qid=Q705916}} in Owari, they passed through Mino and reached Kuroda Shrine.
*They stopped their palanquin in the forest of Kuroda Shrine and spent the night inside. It was the full-moon night of lunar August 15. Villagers treated them kindly with dishes of {{ill|Taro|Q227997|qid=Q227997}}. In thanks, the princes offered dew from taro leaves to Kuroda Shrine, prayed for villagers’ happiness, and departed before dawn.
